fieldMarks: Long, well-furred body, short legs and a full tail about one-third of total length.
Dark to chocolate-brown fur; black tail, legs and rump; grizzled gold and silver on back and shoulders.
Males much larger than females (males 7–15 lb, females 4–9 lb).
behavior: Opportunistic carnivore hunting on the forest floor and in the canopy: squirrels, chipmunks, mice, porcupines, plus insects, fruit and fungi.
One of the few predators that regularly kills porcupines.
Kits born late February to May, typically March–April, in tree cavities.
habitat: Forest with overhead cover and abundant downed wood or other structure on the forest floor; increasingly uses fragmented, human-altered forest in the Northeast.
range: Boreal and northern forests of Canada and the northern US. In the Northeast, populations have recovered through natural expansion and reintroductions (West Virginia 1969, New York 1979, Pennsylvania 1994–1998).
